source_refs.note: 3- ZW–ZZ System of Sex Determination: a main subheading of Systems of Sex Determination, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 104-105.

blocks.text: This sex determination is common in birds. The autosome number differs in different birds but the sex chromosomes are ZW in females and ZZ in males. It means that the female bird produces two kinds of eggs; half with Z chromosome and half with W chromosome. While, the all sperms of the male have Z chromosome. When an Z carrying egg is fertilized by the sperm, offspring is male. When a Y carrying egg is fertilized by the sperm, offspring is female.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints “a Y carrying egg”. Birds have no Y chromosome: in the ZW–ZZ system the egg that gives a female (ZW) carries the W chromosome, so it should read “a W carrying egg”.

blocks.alt: Three panels in one row. Humans (XX-XY system): female 44 + XX, male 44 + XY; female gametes X, X and male gametes X, Y give XX, XY, XX, XY. Grasshopper (XX-XO system): female 22 + XX, male 22 + X-; male gametes X and - (no sex chromosome) give XX and X-. Chicken (ZW-ZZ system): female 76 + ZW, male 76 + ZZ; female gametes Z, W and male gametes Z, Z give ZZ and ZW. Female offspring are shaded green, male pink.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.13: Sex determination in animals (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.13).
blocks.long_description: Each panel has a 2 x 2 grid: Female gametes down the side, Male gametes across the top.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 18.13 gives the female grasshopper as 22 + XY. In the XX-XO system the female is 22 + XX, so it is drawn as 22 + XX above. The printed chicken grid also shades ZZ in the female colour and ZW in the male colour; here ZW (female) is green and ZZ (male) pink, as in the other two panels.
